findings.statement: A short/long-distance and cyclic-clock equation improves completed-trip duration prediction in a reserved quarter against the frozen matched controls.

reliability.rationale: The selected two-distance-regime reference has mean daily MAE 9.453892 minutes versus matched robust domain 10.156146 and robust flexible 10.269022 on 92 held pickup days. Worst-day error also improves. A later candidate with lower confirmation error is correctly not promoted.

mechanism.rationale: Actual trip distance is a post-trip measurement. The task is retrospective duration reconstruction, not pickup-time ETA. Airport, borough and time-of-day effects are descriptive route and demand associations; provider reporting quality and missing traffic information preclude a causal travel-time law.

novelty.rationale: Known source analyses and standard mathematical/statistical families are disclosed. This review does not certify a new law or exhaustive novelty.

significance.rationale: A useful compact transportation-response model with fair robust controls and substantial chronological coverage, bounded by one city, one service class and retrospective inputs.

reproducibility.rationale: Native adapter, frozen equations, coefficients and compact evidence were inspected. Separate computational review performs numerical replay; scientific review is not experimental replication.

impact.rationale: No independent deployed intervention, measured cost benefit or external experimental replication establishes industrial impact.

reliability.rationale: All saved predictions and primary metrics independently reproduce from source-verified inputs, including unfavorable alternatives. Whole-day held-quarter trip duration error improves matched robust controls, conditional on completed-trip distance. This information is retrospective and cannot support an operational pickup-time ETA or route optimization claim.
